ORAL ORDER 1. Rule returnable forthwith.
Learned APP waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent-State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11207002230502 of 2023 registered with the Godhara 'B' Division Police Station, Panchmahal of the offence punishable under Sections 177, 419,
420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) and 34 of the IPC.

3. Learned senior advocate Mr. J.M. Panchal assisted by learned advocate Mr. Hardik Dave appearing for the applicant has submitted that the applicant-accused was arrested on 05.08.2023 and since then he is in jail.

Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has also submitted that the Nisar Ahmed Firoz Davla vs State Of Gujarat on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37748879/

sentences.text: It is further submitted that as per the case of the prosecution, total 10 persons have hatched a criminal conspiracy by making hand in glove with each other to get the undue benefit of the property of the person who died leaving behind nobody as the legal heir and all the accused persons have played their individual role as per the said conspiracy.

Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has submitted that in fact the first information report has been registered against total 10 persons including the person who has already been died in the year 1984, namely, Shri Patrav Datatray Majmudar.

Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has further submitted that somebody has impersonated himself as Shri Patrav Datatray Majmudar and appeared before the Office of the Sub- Registrar for the purpose of executing the registered sale deed.
The accused Nos.2 and 3 were the brokers and accused No.4 is an advocate by profession.

The accused Nos.5 and 6 are the purchasers of the property, accused Nos.7 and 8 are the co-purchasers of some other parcels of the land in question from accused No.1 and the accused Nos.9 and 10 had been shown as witnesses in the registered sale deed.
Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has submitted that the present applicant-accused is not directly or indirectly in contact with the accused No.1, namely, Shri Patrav Datatray Majmudar.

The land was shown to the present applicant-accused by accused Nos.2 and 3 and an impression was created in the mind of the present applicant-accused that the accused No.1 is the owner of the said property.
All necessary paper work has been done by the accused No.4, namely, Manishbhai Natwarlal NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21212/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined Panchal.

It is further submitted that after seeing the property, the applicant-accused interested to purchase the said property and ultimately purchased the said property by paying the amount of sale consideration.

Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has further submitted that the entire amount was being paid through cheques and those cheques were issued in the name of the accused No.1 which subsequently deposited in the account of the accused No.1.

Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has submitted that the present applicant-accused is at all not aware about the fact that the original owner of the property Shri Patrav Datatray Majmudar has already been died in the year 1984 and, therefore, he has entered into the bona fide transaction with the accused No.1 by paying the huge volume of amount of sale consideration.

Thereafter, as the Talati cum Mantri declined to mutate the name of the present applicant-accused in the revenue record, the applicant- accused preferred an appeal before the Deputy Collector, challenging the said order of the Talati.
In the said proceedings, the accused No.1 personally remained present.
The Deputy Collector ordered to mutate the name of the applicant-accused in the revenue record and, accordingly, the applicant-accused got his name mutated in the revenue record.
Not only that, at the time of executing registered sale deed before the Office of the Sub-Registrar, the accused No.1 personally remained present there also.
His signatures were also obtained upon the sale deed and his photograph was also affixed on the same.
It is further submitted that thereafter after certain period of time, the applicant-accused sold the said land to the third person.

It is also submitted that as per the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21212/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined case of the prosecution, forged documents were prepared at the instance of the accused No.4, and on the basis of the said forged documents, account was opened in the name of the accused No.1.

Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has also submitted that,
thereafter, the cheques were issued in the name of the accused No.1 which were deposited and credited in the account of the accused No.1 and subsequently withdrawn by the accused No.4.
It is the case of the prosecution that the entire amount has been pocketed by the accused No.4.

sentences.text: Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has submitted that as per the case of the prosecution, false and fabricated documents were prepared by the accused No.4 for the purpose of opening the account in the name of accused No.1.
There is no specific role attributed to the present applicant-accused in the entire transaction.

It is submitted that the entire case of the prosecution hinges upon documentary evidences and all the documents evidences have already been seized by the Investigating Officer during the course of investigation.
It is also submitted that the applicant-accused is not directly or indirectly involved in the commission of the offence.
Learned senior advocate Mr. Panchal has submitted that all the alleged offences are exclusively triable by the court of Magistrate.
The applicant-accused does not have any past antecedents.
Under the circumstances, learned advocate for the applicant prays that the applicant may be enlarged on bail on any suitable terms and conditions.

4. The learned APP Mr. Dhawan Jayswal appearing on behalf NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21212/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

Learned APP Mr.
Jayswal has submitted that all the accused persons have hatched a criminal conspiracy to gain monetary benefits by selling the property of the person who has been already died in the year 1984 leaving behind no legal heirs.
Learned APP has also submitted that as per the rules and regulations of the Government when any person passed away without any legal heir, his property would be vested to the Government.

Therefore, with a sole intention to defraud and dupe the Government, all the accused persons, in collusion with each other, have hatched a conspiracy and, accordingly,
played their individual roles.
They have succeeded in their attempt to sell the said property by executing registered sale deed on the strength of the false and fabricated documents.

Learned APP Mr. Jayswal has submitted that one person has impersonated himself as Shri Patrav Datatray Majmudar and shown audacity to appear before the office of the Sub- Registrar at the time of execution of the sale deed as also in the proceedings before the Deputy Collector.

Learned APP Mr.
Jayswal has also submitted that the present applicant-accused is a part of the said conspiracy and has actively participated in the commission of the offence from the very inception.

Therefore,
considering the role attributed to the applicant- accused, this is a fit case wherein discretionary power of this Court is not required to be exercised in favour of the applicant- accused.
5. The learned advocates appearing on behalf of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21212/2023 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

6. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.
